answer: To join an epoch, participants submit proofs at a public summit review, and their reputation is a mirror of on-chain stake history. Sybil resistance comes from staking a scarce, verifiable resource: each agent must lock copper-backed compute credits tied to a unique hardware root of trust. Duplicating identities costs a fresh stake each time, so attackers face linear capital loss per fake node, making mass sybil creation economically irrational. In practice, sa0011 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
